verdict.rationale: Zulip's own documented topic model gives each side conversation in a channel its own topic. Community users credit this threading model and say threads can be created 'on the fly from existing messages', but the docs never describe replying to a specific message so the thread stays attached to it. Usability complaints (e.g. posting to an unexpected thread) are UX caveats, not a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of replying from a specific message into a thread anchored to that original message, and documentation of the reply/thread UI flow.

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can reply in threads so side discussions stay attached to the original message

citations.quote: Lots of conversations can happen in the same channel at the same time, each in its own topic. You never have to worry about interrupting — each conversation has its own space.
In Zulip you can create threads on the fly from existing messages
The most important feature of Zulip is threading.
